primitives.name: Opponent-Adjusted Pass EPA
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each 2025 team-week, pass EPA per attempt minus that opponent's 2025 defensive pass EPA per attempt, weighted by attempts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EPA_{t,i}': 'expected points added for team t in week i', 'DefEPA_{o(i),i}': 'defensive expected points added for opponent o(i) in week i', 'Attempts_{t,i}': 'number of passing attempts by team t in week i'}
primitives.assumptions: 2025 defensive metrics are stable and representative; opponent adjustments are linear in time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When opponent's defensive EPA exceeds offensive EPA, resulting in negative values.

layer2.mapping: Used as a component in the `on_field_efficiency` blend, representing isolated offensive pass performance relative to opponent strength.
layer2.telemetry: Difference between observed and expected pass EPA, adjusted for opponent.

primitives.name: On-Field Efficiency Blend
primitives.verbatim_quote: The signed home-minus-away blend, clipped to [-1, 1]: - 55% opponent-adjusted pass EPA - 15% opponent-adjusted rush EPA - 15% CPOE - 10% explosive pass rate (20+ air yards) - 5% interception luck, sign flipped so fewer interceptions than the league rate is positive That blend is `on_field_efficiency`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'OAdjPassEPA': 'opponent-adjusted pass EPA', 'OAdjRushEPA': 'opponent-adjusted rush EPA', 'CPOE': 'completion percentage over expected', 'ExplosivePassRate': 'proportion of passes with 20+ air yards', 'InterceptionLuck': 'interceptions below league average (sign-flipped)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear combination weights are fixed; all inputs are normalized and clipped to [-1, 1].
primitives.breakdown_regime: When any component is extreme, leading to clipping or dominance of one term.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE’s internal efficiency kernel, used for state transition modeling in situational play analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized composite metric of team performance across multiple efficiency dimensions.

primitives.name: Home-Away Bias Adjustment
primitives.verbatim_quote: The signed home-minus-away blend, clipped to [-1, 1]: - 55% opponent-adjusted pass EPA - 15% opponent-adjusted rush EPA - 15% CPOE - 10% explosive pass rate (20+ air yards) - 5% interception luck, sign flipped so fewer interceptions than the league rate is positive That blend is `on_field_efficiency`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'HomeEfficiency': 'average efficiency when playing at home', 'AwayEfficiency': 'average efficiency when playing away'}
primitives.assumptions: Home field advantage is additive and quantifiable via historical efficiency differentials.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When home or away efficiency is undefined due to insufficient data.

layer2.mapping: Applied as a scalar modifier in GSE’s state-space model to reflect environmental influence on performance.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in efficiency between home and away games, clipped to [-1,1].

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that raw efficiency metrics like EPA are inherently biased by opponent strength. To isolate true team capability, opponent-adjusted metrics are computed by subtracting opponent defensive averages from team offensive averages, weighted by attempts. This creates a normalized measure of performance. The `on_field_efficiency` primitive then combines these adjusted metrics with other key indicators such as CPOE, explosive pass rate, and interception luck into a single scalar. Each component is weighted according to its predictive value. The inclusion of a home-away bias ensures that environmental factors are accounted for. The process avoids overfitting by excluding current season data in the baseline and applying shrinkage. The final blend is clipped to [-1,1] to prevent extreme outliers from skewing predictions. This approach enables both GSI to compute probabilistic rankings and GSE to model state transitions in real-time.
